subject: Acme POC — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir.khanna@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer support assistant (FAQ + triage) at production scale.
- Primary success metrics discussed: latency (p95), answer accuracy/quality on a curated eval set, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Data flow: requests hit Acme frontend -> shadow to Redwood -> responses returned to Acme for evaluation (no customer-facing changes initially).

Proposed next steps / POC plan (attached):
1) Confirm success criteria (we sketched numbers below)
2) We run a 2-week offline eval (curated prompts + human grading) to iterate on prompts and model config
3) Follow with a 2-week online shadow run to validate latency and integration behavior
4) Decision point & recommendation review with stakeholders

Draft success criteria (please confirm or adjust):
- Functional accuracy: >= 85% acceptable answers on curated eval set (per agreed rubric)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for typical support queries (95th percentile)
- Cost: target cost per 1M tokens below $120 (TBD based on traffic profile)

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood: Dylan Brooks (evals methodology & instrumentation), Rachel Kim (infra/provisioning)
- Acme: Jordan Lee (PM), Samir Khanna (integration owner)

I've attached our initial POC plan and an eval criteria template (redwood-acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf, eval-criteria-template.xlsx). Can you confirm the owners and the success criteria? If that looks good, I'll schedule a kickoff for the week of June 7 and loop in engineering.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: redwood-acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf (13 KB), eval-criteria-template.xlsx (8 KB)

Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 17:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side after chatting with Jordan: 

Success criteria feedback:
- Accuracy: 85% acceptable answers on the curated set seems reasonable as a starting point. We'll expect to iterate.
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms is a hard target for the first phase; if shadow shows higher p95 we may need fallback rules.
- Cost: the $120/1M tokens target is a placeholder — Jordan will share expected monthly token volume so we can model costs.

Evals methodology: Jordan and I prefer starting with offline evals (rapid iteration), then moving to an online shadow for a short production validation. Two questions: 
1) Can we run a parallel online shadow with sampling (no customer-facing outputs) to measure p95 without full traffic?
2) For the grading rubric, can you share examples of the scoring scale (what constitutes a 3 vs 2 for correctness)?

Owners: confirmed — Jordan (PM), Samir (integration), Dylan & Rachel for Redwood.

If you can provide a slightly more detailed grading rubric and a refined timeline, we'll be ready to kick off the week of June 7. Also, Jordan will send over expected traffic volume later today.

Best,
Samir
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Corp
samir.khanna@acme.com

Hi Samir / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick response and alignment on owners. Per your questions, below is a recommended approach and a sample grading rubric to unblock the offline evals quickly. We'll attach a revised POC plan (minor edits) and a sample rubric in Drive.

Recommended evaluation approach (hybrid):
- Week 1-2: Offline evals (curated prompts + human graders) to tune prompts, temperature, guardrails, and evaluate semantic correctness.
- Week 3-4: Online shadow (sampled traffic) to validate latency, throughput, and integration behavior. No customer-visible changes during shadow.
- Decision checkpoint: End of Week 4 — review metrics + qualitative feedback and recommend next steps.

Online shadow details:
- We can run a 10-20% sample of incoming support traffic proxied to Redwood in shadow mode (no writes to downstream systems) to measure p95 and behaviour.
- Redwood will provide tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown for the shadow period.

Sample grading rubric (offline human grading) — each query graded 0-3 unless noted:
- Correctness (0-3): 3 = fully correct and actionable, 2 = mostly correct with minor omissions, 1 = partial or misleading, 0 = incorrect
- Hallucination flag (0-1): 1 = obvious hallucination, 0 = no hallucination
- Relevance (0-2): 2 = directly relevant, 1 = partially relevant, 0 = irrelevant
- Tone/compliance (0-2): 2 = acceptable, 1 = borderline, 0 = unacceptable

Scoring: normalization and pass threshold will be applied across these axes (e.g., weighted score >= 0.75 pass threshold — we can refine weights).

Owners (confirmed):
- Redwood lead: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.com) — responsible for evals methodology, rubric, and grading coordination.
- Redwood infra: Rachel Kim (rachel.kim@redwood.com) — responsible for provisioning shadow environment and tracing integration.
- Acme leads: Jordan Lee (PM), Samir Khanna (integration lead)

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll update the POC plan with the hybrid timeline and rubric and share the Drive folder (link below).
2) Jordan to share expected monthly token volume so we can firm up cost targets.
3) If you confirm kickoff week of June 7, we'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with engineering (Dylan & Rachel).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-eval-poc
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/ACME-12345

I'll send a revised plan shortly. Thanks —
Marissa
